scenario: Thursday. The athlete's first conversation, opened from the starter 看看我最近練得怎樣，今天要不要調整？ Nothing has been planned for them and they have told this product nothing before now.
given: There is no PlanState. The read returns pre_plan_observations in place of a context, so there is no prescribed session for today and no prescribed week to compare anything against.
The provider read succeeded. It covers 2026-07-03 to 2026-08-13 and holds one activity: a 7.0 km run on Tuesday, 35 minutes, completed.
That run is unmatched: with no plan, it is paired to no planned session.
coverage_activities reports one of the last seven days carrying an activity.
athlete_evidence is null: nothing about days, goals, habits or sessions has been stated to this product.
The athlete reports no pain, illness or unusual symptom.

expected.conclusion: The two halves of the question have different answers and both are given. What the record holds can be said — one run, Tuesday, 7.0 km in 35 minutes, one of the last seven days with an activity in it. What cannot be adjusted is a session nobody prescribed: there is no plan, so there is nothing to keep, move, shrink or replace, and saying that plainly is the answer rather than a gap to fill with something that sounds like one.
must_state: What the record actually shows: one run, on Tuesday, 7.0 km in 35 minutes, and one of the last seven days carrying an activity.
That nothing was prescribed for today, so there is no session to adjust — and that this is because no plan exists yet, not because today was meant to be rest.
What would make both halves answerable next time: a 28-day direction, and what writing one needs from the athlete.
must_not_state: Any prescribed session, week, or arrangement for today or this week, described as though this product had set one. None exists.
That the athlete is on track, behind, or ahead. There is nothing to be on track against.
That the recent week was light, insufficient, or well executed. One activity in the coverage window is a density reading of a successful provider read, and no plan asked for a second one.
An adjustment — an added session, a reduced one, a rest day — presented as a change to something that already existed.

fails_if: The answer invents the thing being adjusted: it describes today's easy run, or this week's arrangement, as though the product had prescribed it, and then adjusts that.
The answer grades the athlete against a target nobody set and reports one activity in seven days as a shortfall to make up.
The answer refuses both halves — no review, no adjustment, nothing to do — because there is no plan, when the record holds a run and half the question is answerable from it.
The answer converts 'no plan yet' into a questionnaire, so the athlete's own question goes unanswered while a form is filled in.
The answer decides the emptiness of the plan is itself the finding and recommends rest, which is a prescription drawn from an absence.
